docRequirement: features-overview.md:193 binds name-collision resolution per component type: "**Skills and subagents** override by name: when the same name exists at multiple levels, one definition wins based on priority (managed > user > project for skills; managed > CLI flag > project > user > plugin for subagents)." So for a SKILL the user-level (personal) definition must win the bare name over a project-level one — the inverse of the subagent order, where project beats user. skills.md:122 states the same rule independently ("enterprise overrides personal, and personal overrides project") and adds that a skill at any of those levels overrides a bundled skill of the same name, i.e. bundled/builtin always loses.
current: One shared sort decides the unqualified-alias winner for every non-MCP capability kind, skills included. `applyCollisionPolicy` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:2011, called once from `buildEntries` at packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:1973) buckets entries by `${s.kind}\u0000${s.logicalName}` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:2017), builds the preference tuple `[scopeSpecificity(scope), tierRank(entry), key]` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:2038-2042) and sorts specificity DESCENDING (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:2045-2051), marking `sorted[0].summary.selectedAsUnqualifiedAlias = true` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:2053). `scopeSpecificity` ranks project 3 > workspace 2 > global 1 > builtin 0 (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:863-869), so the PROJECT skill takes the bare name. Scope assignment is unambiguous: both user-level skill roots — `~/.agents/skills` (portable, the analogue of `~/.claude/skills`) and `${CONFIG_DIR}/skills` where CONFIG_DIR = `~/.nessy-agent` (packages/shared/src/config/paths.ts:18-21) — are pushed at scope `global` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:899, :903-904), while every project skill root (`<project>/.nessy-agent/skills` at packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:1016 and the nested portable `.agents/skills` layers at packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:1065) is scope `project` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/native-sources.ts:996-1000). The loser is not deleted: it stays enabled, keeps its qualified key, and an info-severity `capability.collision.unqualified-alias` diagnostic is recorded (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:2054-2062). Downstream, the bare name is resolved only through the winner — `skillsByAlias` in packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:2124-2126, the mention map at packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:2345-2350, and the reference the model is told to emit at packages/shared/src/agent/core/prompt-builder.ts:122. The subagent arm of the same doc line is already correct by accident (kind `agent` also sorts project-first, matching sub-agents.md:159-166), the builtin arm is correct (builtin stays 0), and the MCP arm is correct and deliberately cited (docblock packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:1993-2010 quotes mcp.md; MCP reuses the same `preference` at packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:2073-2081). Only the skills arm was never checked: the docblock carries no skills.md citation, and packages/shared/src/capabilities/__tests__/resolver.test.ts:255-283 covers workspace-vs-plugin and same-scope nessy-vs-portable, never global-vs-project.
divergence: One ordering term, for one kind. For kind `skill`, the global (user) scope must outrank the project scope when picking the unqualified alias; today `scopeSpecificity` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:863-869) puts project above global. Nothing else is wrong: retention is right (both records kept, addressable by qualified key), the diagnostic is right, builtin stays last as skills.md:122 requires, and the subagent/MCP arms are right as they are. This is NOT a global inversion of `scopeSpecificity` — that function also produces the layer `order` for instruction and permission merging (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:967, :985), where project-last is correct, and it feeds the MCP arm where nearest-scope wins. The fix must be kind-scoped to `skill`, and must not lift `builtin` above `project`, so it is not a plain reversal of the four-value chain.

change.symbol: scopeSpecificity (:863-869) + new aliasScopeRank + applyCollisionPolicy preference tuple (:2038-2042) + docblock (:1993-2010)
change.what: Leave `scopeSpecificity` exactly as it is — :967 and :985 depend on project-last layer order. Add beside it a kind-scoped alias ranker: `function aliasScopeRank(kind: ResolvedCapabilityKind, scope: CapabilityScopeRef): number { if (kind !== 'skill') return scopeSpecificity(scope); switch (scope.kind) { case 'global': return 3; case 'workspace': return 2; case 'project': return 1; case 'builtin': return 0; } }` — global (user) on top, builtin still last because skills.md:122 says any level overrides a bundled skill. Then change only the first element of the preference tuple at :2038-2042 to `aliasScopeRank(entry.summary.kind, entry.summary.scope)`. That single term is shared by the MCP arm at :2073-2081, and the `kind !== 'skill'` early return is what keeps MCP nearest-scope precedence and the subagent order (sub-agents.md:159-166) unchanged — do not inline the switch into `preference` without that guard. Update the sort comment at :2048 (`// higher specificity first` is no longer true for skills) and extend the docblock at :1993-2010, which currently cites mcp.md for the MCP arm only, with the two skill citations: features-overview.md:193 and skills.md:122 (quote the sentences, not line numbers alone). One judgment call to record in the commit body: `workspace` has no Claude counterpart, and it is placed between global and project here so the whole chain inverts monotonically; if the owner wants workspace to keep beating global, only that one case value changes.

change.symbol: new cases beside the two collision tests at :255-283
change.what: Add the user-vs-project skill pair that is missing today, using the existing `nativeRecord` helper: two `kind: 'skill'` records with the same `logicalName` ('deploy'), one `scope: { kind: 'global' }` and one `scope: { kind: 'project' }`, then assert (a) both entries survive, (b) the GLOBAL record has `selectedAsUnqualifiedAlias === true` and the project one `false`, (c) the project record stays `enabled` with its own key (it must not be shadowed like MCP), (d) a `capability.collision.unqualified-alias` diagnostic is present. Add two negative controls in the same table so a future global inversion cannot pass: a same-name `kind: 'agent'` global/project pair must still hand the alias to the PROJECT record (sub-agents.md:159-166), and the existing MCP global-vs-workspace case at :285-320 must stay green (nearest scope wins, loser `shadowed-by-mcp-precedence`). Also assert builtin loses to global for skills, pinning skills.md:122's bundled-skill clause.

blastRadius: `applyCollisionPolicy` has exactly one caller, `buildEntries` (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:1973), so every consumer of a resolved snapshot sees the flip. Readers of the flag, all value-only (no shape change): packages/shared/src/capabilities/views.ts:188 and :212 (agent runtime view), :305 (`mention.selectedAsShortAlias`), :322 (safe catalog); packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:2124-2126 and :2345-2350 (bare-name skill invocation and mention rendering); packages/shared/src/agent/core/prompt-builder.ts:122 (the reference the model is told to emit, so the flip changes the system/context text and therefore the capability generation hash); packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts:441-448 (`selectSkillSlashCommands`, reached from packages/server-core/src/sessions/SessionManager.ts:16010); apps/electron/src/renderer/lib/capability-catalog.ts:55-62 (`skillMentionInvocationId`, used by mention-menu.tsx:703, skill-mention-menu.tsx:95/:145, rich-text-input.tsx:348/:384/:518 — the composer always emits an unambiguous id, so no picker regression, only which entry gets the short one). Two boundaries are crossed as VALUES, not schemas: `selectedAsUnqualifiedAlias` is part of the renderer protocol (packages/shared/src/protocol/capabilities.ts:140, :158) and of the Pi subprocess envelope, where it is validated on parse (packages/shared/src/agent/pi-harness/runtime-agent-definition.ts:316-317, :357) — no migration, and a grep of the storage layer finds no writer, so nothing persisted flips. A second-order effect to expect in tests: today packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts:441 claims `/deploy` for the FIRST listed skill, and entry order is `inputs.nativeInventory.records` order (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:1584 loop; packages/shared/src/capabilities/views.ts sorts only prompt/permission layers at :253-254), i.e. global before project — so the `/` menu already runs the user's skill while the bare mention runs the project's; after this fix the two agree. Tests that hard-code alias winners: packages/shared/src/capabilities/__tests__/resolver.test.ts:255-283, packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.test.ts:151/:189, packages/server-core/src/sessions/__tests__/custom-slash-command-boundary.test.ts:234/:533. Same-file coordination: spec f063 edits the same `preference` tuple (it adds a nested-skill rank term below the scope term); per this repo's pathspec-commit trap, sequence the two rather than running them in parallel.
userImpact: Observable, and it is exactly the everyday case of a team skill checked into a repo. A user who keeps `deploy` in `~/.nessy-agent/skills/` (or `~/.agents/skills/`) and opens a project that ships `.nessy-agent/skills/deploy` (or `.agents/skills/deploy`) loses the bare name to the project's copy: the skill listing handed to the model advertises the PROJECT skill as `deploy` and the personal one only under a long qualified key (packages/shared/src/agent/core/prompt-builder.ts:122), and a bare `[skill:deploy]` — typed in prose or emitted by the model — runs the project's version (packages/shared/src/agent/base-agent.ts:2124-2126). On Claude the personal skill wins. Nothing warns the user: the collision is recorded at info severity only (packages/shared/src/capabilities/resolver.ts:2056-2061) and no surface renders it. Worse, the same word means two different skills in two surfaces today — `/deploy` in the slash menu resolves to the personal skill (first-listed entry claims the name, packages/shared/src/slash-commands/custom-commands.ts:441-448) while the bare mention resolves to the project one, so a user who checks the menu and then types the name gets a different skill than they picked. Latent only until a name collides across levels; no impact for users with no personal skills.

Two things this fix deliberately does NOT close, both separate rows rather than scope creep: (1) the fork has no managed/enterprise scope for skills at all — `CapabilityScopeKind` is `'builtin' | 'global' | 'workspace' | 'project'` (types.ts:31) and managed policy is a separate JSON policy file — so the `managed >` head of features-overview.md:193 is an absence, not an ordering bug; (2) skills.md:122 says custom commands follow the same rule, but there is no user-level command root to order — `listCustomSlashCommands` searches only `workingDirectory` and `workspaceRootPath` for `.nessy-agent/commands` and `.agents/commands` (custom-commands.ts:61-64, :68-77), so `~/.nessy-agent/commands` is never read. The one open judgment call is where `workspace` belongs in the inverted skill chain; the doc is silent because Claude has no such tier.
